Md Abdus Samad with Md Bazlul Dabir with Shachira Hossain, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
ALM Asaduzzaman, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Abdul Kader Khan ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Rajshahi Co-operative Town Society Ltd ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Rule arises out of an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (Act V of 1908) at the instance of the petitioner-appellant petitioner A Kader Khan and is directed against the judgment and order dated 29-9-1994 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge 1st Court Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 49 of 1986 affirming the order dated 18-1-1996 passed by the learned Rent Controller, Sadar, Rajshahi in (Rent Control) Miscellaneous Case No. 245 of 1983. 

 2. Short facts leading to the disposal of this Rule are that the petitioner instituted the Rent Control Case No. 245 of 1983 before the Controller against the opposite party with the prayer to make necessary repairing works and construction of room No. 9 and also for taking proper measures in making repairs and maintenance of latrine and water lines within the reasonable time to be directed by the court to make the case premises usable and habitable failing which those works will be completed with the cost of the petitioner and the cost so incurred will be recovered from the opposite party from the monthly rent of the said premises with an estimation of Taka 21,935/69. It is also the petitioner’s case that he took lease of the room Nos. 7-9 from the Co-operative Mansion belonging to the opposite party on the basis of an agreement dated 1-2-1975 at a monthly rental if Taka 110 and that these three rooms are contiguous and adjacent to each other being connected by a wooden door. The room No. 9 is situated in the eastern side and the said room is provided with latrine and water connection. The petitioner was carrying on medicine business under the name and style "Paradise Medical." He was in need of latrine and water supply. It is also the case of the petitioner that due to the acquisition of north-east side of room No.9 by the RTDA for the development of Rajshahi Nawbabganj road the said room was dismantled along with the sanitary latrine in the month of January, 1983. Consequently, room No. 9 has become unfit for use and the security of room Nos. 7 and 8 has become hampered. The petitioner then applied to the opposite party for making the room fit for use by construction and providing with water and latrine facilities but the latter declined to discharge their obligation stating that the petitioner has no leasehold right in respect of the room No. 9 of the tenanted premises. Hence, the petitioner was constrained to file the application under section 21(3) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance before the Controller. 

 3. The opposite party entered appearance by filing a written objection denying all the allegations of the petitioner. It has been alleged in the written statement that the case premises along with other rooms were let out to the petitioner at a rental of Taka 110. Subsequently, as per agreement dated 1-7-1979 the rent was increased at Taka 135. It has been further alleged that the sanitary latrine was not included in the agreement. The latrine was meant for use by the employees and other tenants but due to acquisition of the room No.9 by the RTDA there is no existence of the said room in the case premises and in view of the acquisition rental for the room Nos. 7 and 8 was again reduced from Taka 135 to Taka 110 on 8-9-1983. But the petitioner did not pay any rental up to the month of September, 1983. Thereafter, a sub-committee was formed at the instance of the Registrar, Co-operative Society which recommended for 50% increase of the rental of all the tenanted premises including the petitioner one. Thereafter, in consequence of raising objection by the tenants 35% of the rental was increased and accordingly, the rental of the room Nos. 7 and 8 was fixed at Taka 110 with effect from October, 1983 but the petitioner without paying the rental from the month of September, 1983 as per the increased rent filed this application. 

 7. Mr Md Abdus Samad, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits frankly that the case premises is vacant and being used by the outsiders and is not fit for use without reconstruction. 

 8. Mr AKM Asaduzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party, however, supports the decision of the Courts below, stating that the same is based on reason and evidence on record. He further submits that the petitioner was not competent to make an application for repair remaining out of possession in the case premises due to dismantling and, as such, the Court below committed no error in law in his decision. 

 Admittedly, the petitioner was out of possession of the case premises due to dismantling of the room No. 9 at the date of making the application under section 21(3) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, 986. 

 11. But according to the section 21(1) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance it requires for the tenant before making an application under the section 21 (3) he is to be in possession of the tenanted premises. It is, thus, apparently clear that an application under section 21(3) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, is incompetent in law in case the tenant making the application remains out of possession. 

 12. Now, in the instant case what we find is that the tenant i.e. the petitioner was not in possession of the tenanted premises at the relevant time of making the application. The learned courts below while deciding the case did not notice this position in law. Secondly, I do not differ with the decision arrived at by both the Courts below to the effect that the case premises cannot be made usable without reconstruction but the reconstruction is not permitted by the provisions as contained in section 21 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. 

 13. In the facts of the case and having regard to the position of law as discussed above, I am of the view in the following. "That no application under section 21(3) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance is maintainable in the case when the tenant seeking permission is out of possession at the relevant time of making the application and when the question of reconstruction is involved." In that view of the matter it reveals that the courts below committed no error of law in dismissing the application as made by the petitioner. Thus, the Rule bears no merit. 

 15. The judgment and order dated 29-9-1994 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 49 of 1986 affirming the order dated 18-1-1986 passed by the Rent Controller Rajshahi, Sadar in (Rent Control) Miscellaneous Case No. 245 of 1983 is confirmed.
